blocks.text: Born in San Francisco to Serbian emigrants, Jovan studies at Kiev and Saint Petersburg. He receives monastic tonsure and diaconal ordination in 1887 and returns to the United States, later serving as priest under Bishop Nicholas.

blocks.text: The Canadian historical biography expands the North American setting: church schools, teaching, worship, and journeys among scattered communities. It describes travel to the Pacific Northwest and Canada and the effort to organize congregations without a settled priest. Its date styles are not silently converted into a competing civil calendar.

blocks.text: The OCA credits him with the first Serbian parish in America, at Jackson in 1894. Under Tikhon he works in mission administration and preaches in English, Serbian, and Russian. Later journeys take him repeatedly across the Atlantic and Pacific.

blocks.text: The Canadian account describes English portions at the dedication of Saint Sava’s church in Jackson and further work in Seattle, Wilkeson, Butte, and Alaska. It also follows the Serbian mission within the wider North American diocese. This places national pastoral care alongside cooperation under the missionary bishops.

blocks.text: He spends his final years at Žića and reposes in 1940. The OCA gives November 17/30, preserving both printed dates. His relics are returned to Jackson in 2007. No martyrdom by execution is reported.

blocks.text: Dabovich’s own 1898 preface addresses Orthodox brethren and children in the English-speaking world. He offers lives of saints together with lectures and sermons for devotional family reading and school use. He says he wishes the recorded lives themselves to speak and identifies Scripture and the early Fathers as the foundation of his instruction. This is evidence of his publishing purpose in his own lifetime, distinct from a later canonization biography. The surviving scan also identifies him as compiler and translator and locates publication at the Murdock Press in San Francisco. Its dedication remembers Metropolitan Isidore’s support for the young North American Church. Broken words in the retained OCR are summarized rather than quietly repaired into an allegedly verbatim quotation.
